hero.label: Made for Blaze
hero.headline: I want to help Blaze make cross-border payments borderless for everyone.
hero.subheadline: The idea of building a global Venmo hits close to home for me. As a Spanish-speaking student with roots across borders, I know firsthand how broken international money movement still is. Blaze is tackling something genuinely hard, and I want to be part of the team doing it.

whyCompany.title: Cross-border payments is a massive, underserved market finally ready to move
whyCompany.body: Billions of dollars flow across borders every day through slow, expensive, opaque systems. Positioning Blaze as the global Venmo is the right framing at the right moment, as mobile-first financial behavior becomes the norm worldwide. The opportunity to own that category is real and the window is open right now.

whyCompany.title: Early-stage means every rep, every deal, and every conversation actually matters
whyCompany.body: At this stage, a BD intern is not a support function but a core part of figuring out what works. The outreach I run, the objections I handle, and the prospects I convert will directly shape how Blaze builds its go-to-market motion. That kind of leverage is exactly where I do my best work.

whyCompany.title: My BDR track record maps directly onto what Blaze needs right now
whyCompany.body: At Copygen.ai I ran cold outreach end to end using HubSpot and LinkedIn sequences and helped bring in 15 to 20 paying clients from scratch. Most recently at NextAfter I sharpened my ability to communicate value in crowded B2B markets where trust is everything. That combination of pipeline-building muscle and messaging discipline is exactly what early BD at a fintech startup demands.

quote: I grew up watching family members pay absurd fees just to send money home. When I saw Blaze described as a global Venmo, I did not think about the role first. I thought about how badly this product needs to exist.
